summary: Wi‑Fi AP certificate chain mismatch causes 802.1X failures and downstream VPN SSO timeouts for new onboarded devices
description:
Issue summary:
Several newly provisioned employee laptops (macOS 13/14, Windows 11) report repeated 802.1X authentication failures when connecting to corporate SSID (Redwood-Corp). Affected devices subsequently fail to establish VPN SSO sessions (Okta SAML) when automated onboarding attempts to complete, resulting in access failures to internal services (Confluence, Jira, internal APIs).

Impact:
- New hires during onboarding can't complete account setup or access internal tooling.
- Ticket volume increased in #it-helpdesk and #onboarding with ~12 reported devices in two days.
- Intermittent for existing already-provisioned devices; primarily impacts devices re-provisioned or newly enrolled.

Environment:
- Office SSID: Redwood-Corp (WPA2/WPA3 802.1X, EAP-TLS)
- RADIUS cluster: radius-usw-1/2 (running FreeRADIUS 3.2.2) behind haproxy
- APs: Aruba OS 8.10 (provisioned via wifi-config) with recently rotated AP certs on 2026-03-10
- Identity provider: Okta (SAML) region us-west-2

Steps to reproduce:
1) Unbox a laptop and enroll with MDM (Intune).
2) Auto-provision Wi‑Fi profile (EAP-TLS, client cert pushed by MDM).
3) Attempt to join Redwood-Corp SSID — observe repeated EAP-TLS failures.
4) Attempt VPN SSO (Okta) — browser times out on SAML redirect or returns 502 from vpn-terminator.

Observed logs / evidence:
- Radius logs (/var/log/freeradius/radius.log): "TLS: Handshake failed: certificate verify failed: certificate has expired or is not yet valid" on radius-usw-1 when AP bridge presents cert chain.
- AP web management and CLI show AP cert installed on 2026-03-10 with missing intermediate in chain.
- tcpdump at haproxy shows TLS handshake to RADIUS failing with 'unknown_ca' alert from RADIUS side.
- Okta logs show SAML assertion timeouts correlated to client never completing network auth.
- Wireshark capture from macOS dev: EAP-TLS 13 handshake stops at CertificateVerify.
- MDM profile push status shows 200 but clients report "TLS: verify error" in system log.

Initial hypothesis:
A partial/intermediate CA was not included when AP certificates were reissued during last rotation (2026-03-10). APs present an incomplete chain to RADIUS and to client provisioning flows causing EAP-TLS to fail. Because onboarding expects the device to be on the corporate network (Wi‑Fi) to complete the SSO flow, the failure cascades into VPN SSO timeouts and blocked onboarding.

Immediate customer-impact workaround implemented: 
- Float a temporary open onboarding SSID (Redwood-Onboard-Temp) scoped to the SF office with captive portal + limited network access to reach MDM and Okta so new devices can complete provisioning.
- Emergency config change: re-enable legacy fallback for specific MDM-tagged devices to allow WPA2-PSK onboarding while we remediate certs.

Suggested permanent fix: 
- Re-issue AP certs including full cert chain (leaf + intermediate + root) and push to all APs via wifi-config.
- Restart RADIUS instances sequentially after verifying chain verification works locally.
- Add automated verification in wifi-config CI to validate full chain on new certs before rolling.
- Update onboarding runbook to include a fallback SSID and MDM checks during cert rotation windows.
comments: Aisha Patel (IT Helpdesk) 2026-03-12: First reports came from onboarding team — 7 devices failed in SF office. Created ticket and added network/SRE. Placed temporary SSID.

Lina Park (Network Eng) 2026-03-12: Captured radius logs and saw 'certificate verify failed' from radius-usw-1. Suspect intermediate missing on AP certs pushed 03-10. Pulling AP cert on a sample AP now.
Marco Chen (SRE) 2026-03-12: Verified haproxy/tcpdump shows TLS handshake abort. Opened PR in wifi-config to include intermediates in packaging (see related_github_prs).
Ravi Singh (Security) 2026-03-13: Confirmed intermediate CA was rotated last week; chain publishing step failed for one intermediate. Approving reissue. Marked high priority due to onboarding impact.
Onboarding Manager (customer facing) 2026-03-13: Thanks for the temp SSID — got 5 hires through. Please prioritize remediation.
investigation_notes: 03-12 10:40 — Pulled AP cert from ap-sf-12: openssl verify fails locally until we append intermediate.pem.
03-12 11:05 — Reproduced EAP-TLS failure on a test laptop; EAP exchange stops before CertificateVerify.
03-12 13:20 — Confirmed MDM delivered client certs correctly; failure occurs on network auth step (AP/RADIUS).
03-13 09:00 — Checked wifi-config release log: packaging step skipped 'intermediates/' when cert rotation completed. This is likely an automated packaging bug in infra script.
03-13 12:30 — Scoped blast radius to SF and EU offices; APs in APAC had correct chain (rotation earlier completed successfully).
03-13 15:45 — Performed a dry-run reissue for ap-sf-12 with chain included. Radius accepted handshake locally.
resolution: 03-14 07:20 — Reissued AP intermediate certificates with full chain and rolled to SF AP pool via wifi-config PR #142.
03-14 08:10 — Sequentially restarted radius-usw-1 then radius-usw-2 after validation; observed successful EAP-TLS handshakes in logs.
03-14 09:00 — Disabled temporary WPA2-PSK fallback and decommissioned Redwood-Onboard-Temp SSID after confirming 95% of queued devices connected and completed SSO.
03-14 10:30 — Pushed updated MDM profile verification to ensure clients no longer see TLS verify failures.

Follow-up actions: create infra alert for cert chain packaging failures; add CI step to wifi-config to verify chain presence; update Onboarding Runbook with cert-rotation checklist and temporary SSID procedure. Assigned follow-ups to Lina Park and Marco Chen.
next_steps: Write CI check to fail PRs that package AP certs without intermediates (owner: Lina Park).
Add automated synthetic test that performs EAP-TLS handshake against a staging RADIUS instance post-rollout (owner: Marco Chen).
Schedule a postmortem and add to on-call rotation notes; present findings at next weekly infra sync.
Notify HR/onboarding of improved playbook and confirm rollback windows for future rotations.
